beats.t: Dawn spread across the skyship's deck. Beneath the star clouds, a pale golden path had opened where none had been before.
Is that a road? There's a road in the sky.
A road visible only to someone who's recovered their hour. A road home.
Then are you going?
Instead of answering, Yundal raised his gloved hand. The center of the glove sagged inward.
If I go, this hand goes with me. And the people there keep forgetting me. A home where my mother meets her son for the first time, for the third time.
Then you're not going?
I'll decide after breakfast. Hungry people make expensive decisions.
That's true. As a chef, I approve.
Moka lit a small brazier on one side of the deck. He cooked porridge with dew gathered from the star clouds. It smelled simple and warm.
Oink. I mean, that smells good.
You just said oink.
I didn't.
You did. I have recorded it.
Could I get a copy of that record? For blackmail.
When did you two become such friends?!
Smiling, Yundal drew a folded sheet from his clothes. His own Four Pillars chart. New characters sat neatly in the Hour column that had been empty for so long.
It's strange seeing all eight characters filled in. Like wearing someone else's clothes, and like finally wearing clothes that fit.
So what does it say? Your fate.
Wonderful luck with women in my later years. My lady, Moka, would you happen to know your birth—
I'll tip the porridge over.
I'm joking. What it actually says is: someone who lights other people's paths and finds his own late.
That's exactly right at the moment.
Isn't it? I finally believe the saying that fortune-tellers are worst at reading their own fortunes.
You ask for everyone else's birthdays easily enough.
That's business. This is a consultation. No consultation fee.
The four sat around the brazier. Yundal cradled his bowl in both hands. Yeoni watched his hands, then took out their notebook.
Yundal. That's not your real name, is it?
Caught me. How long have you known?
Article Seven. It said you had to state your birth time yourself, but it never asked your name. Blue Rabbit already had your name.
My lady, you should have become an auditor.
Yundal means an extra month inserted into the calendar. A place outside the usual twelve months.
That's right. A month that exists and doesn't. No ancestral rites, no birthdays counted.
Perfect for someone people forget, so I chose it myself. My naming skills are the real thing too.
A brief silence followed his laugh. Charcoal cracked in the brazier. Yeoni put down their pen.
Tell me your real name someday. I'll write it down.
Even written down, it'll be forgotten. The paper will remain, but whoever reads it will wonder: whose name is this?
Then I'll keep reading it. Every time I wonder.
...You really are stubborn.
Always has been. If something tastes bad, they'll say so to the bitter end.
The sky suddenly darkened. Three black hands crawled onto the golden path, chains wrapped around every finger.
The road home lies upon my palm. Try walking it.
You came to block the road? That's low!
No. It didn't come to block the road. It came to watch me. To see whether I go.
Yundal stood and removed his glove. This time he didn't hesitate. A black vortex poured from the hole in his palm.
The three black hands were dragged toward the hole, nails scraping the deck. One, two, three. Each disappeared into it.
The hole has grown. The more of mine you eat, the more you resemble me.
Then I'll eat plenty. Leave you hungry.
Yundal dropped to his knees. Sweat beaded on his forehead. The rim of the hole had spread another finger's length toward his wrist.
Why did you use it again? You said it grows!
I've decided, my lady. I'm not going.
This hole closes only when Black Moon dies. So the quickest way is to stay beside the person heading toward Black Moon.
Then you're staying because of us.
No, because of me. Does putting it that way make you feel less guilty?
After Yeoni and Moka fell asleep in the cabin, Neo called Yundal to the bow. This time, he didn't hide his transparent hand.
One favor.
Mr. Cat asking me? The sun will rise in the west tomorrow.
If I disappear, stay beside them.
Yundal stopped smiling. Below Neo's wrist was empty space. Starlight passed straight through his hand.
Since when?
Since we reached the sky of twelve houses. No, a little before that.
Does my lady know?
They wrote it in their notebook. Neo's hand. Must see it later. I can't leave this until then.
No.
...What did you say?
Our compatibility is wrong. My lady and I. I've checked. Keep your own place, Mr. Cat.
This isn't the time for jokes.
I'm not joking. A guardian whose first thought is to disappear is dangerous. That thought opens a real door.
Neo lowered his head. The edge of his cloak stirred in the wind. Only after a long silence did he speak.
Then just this. If they forget me, remember me. I'm sorry to ask even that of you, when you've always been the forgotten one.
That, I'll accept. A contract between people who are forgotten.
After Neo returned to the cabin, Yundal remained at the bow. A faint moon hung at the edge of the sky, as though leaving a place open for him.
Grandmother. I found my hour. They say I cried before the rooster.
No one answered. Yundal laid his gloved hand over his chest. The hole in his palm seemed to swallow his heartbeat bit by bit.
Not my name yet. I'll find that at the end. My lady says they'll write it down.
A small light shone through the cabin window beneath the deck. Half asleep, Yeoni hugged their notebook.
In the morning, the skyship reached the twelfth house. A door floated among the clouds, old chains wound around its frame.
My lady. Your birth time.
July 6, 2002. Eight thirty in the morning. Mom remembered because her morning drama had just finished.
The number display above the door clicked around. Eight thirty. The chains loosened and fell. The door swung inward.
Inside stretched an endless room of looms. Threads descended from the ceiling and continued beneath the floor. Tiny scenes formed along every thread.
What's this now? A knitting factory?
The twelfth house is the room of endings and hidden things. Here hang the endings of lives other than this one.
Yeoni touched a nearby thread. A scene flashed up: a rainy bus stop. One umbrella. Two pairs of wet sneakers.
Is that me?
Let go. Right now.
At the urgency in Neo's voice, Yeoni released the thread. The scene vanished. Only a rain-soaked chill remained on their fingertips.
(Why is Neo so frightened? Like someone who knows that bus stop.)
Yundal walked slowly between the threads. Near the ceiling, a red star and a blue star floated side by side. Their descending threads twisted into one thick cord.
The two stars in your twelfth house. Mars, the fighting star. Jupiter, the giving star.
Fighting and giving in the same room?
That's why this house is difficult. Hidden enemies are here, and hidden help too. You have to go all the way to the end to know which is which.
Decide before the end and you're usually wrong.
Moka furtively touched another thread. A scene appeared: an unfamiliar kitchen, a steaming pot, someone's laughter. He snatched his paw away.
Didn't see anything. Really. No cooking scenes or anything.
I didn't say a word.
...Guess I cooked in another life too. Never ends.
Deep in the room came the sound of dragging chains, mixed with wet footsteps. Something heavy was being dragged downward.
That way. The chains.
Look at the floor. All the threads go down. Beneath the twelfth house is another sky.
A sky inhabited by twenty-seven moons. The chains are being dragged there.
Then is that the sound we've been following?
No one answered. Instead, the smell of rainwater rose between gaps in the floor. A smell that didn't belong aboard a skyship on a clear day.
Yeoni pressed their stomach. It felt empty inside, like a vessel waiting to be filled.
Follow, vessel. The spring you lost lies below.
I decide my own spring.
The voice didn't answer. Instead, every thread in the floor pulled taut. Something below was tugging on them.
If we go down, can we come back?
Everyone who went down came back. As far as I know. Admittedly, I don't know much.
I'll lead. Yeoni, stay behind me.
No. Beside you.
Neo looked at Yeoni for a moment, then stepped aside. Light from the threads leaked through his transparent fingers.
Yeoni jotted in their notebook: Twelfth house. Below. Chains. Smell of rain. Then they drew a line and added one more thing: Go down together.
